claims.claim: Short-obstruction equivalence and radius-three normal form: in a P8-free bipartite graph, a set S is a feedback vertex set exactly when it meets every induced C4, C6, and C8. Moreover, every component of G-S has radius at most 3; if S is inclusion-minimal, every x in S has two neighbors in one component of G-S.
claims.evidence: The latter clauses are naturally conditional on S being an FVS, as also made explicit in the proof. If G-S is cyclic, a shortest residual cycle is chordless and hence induced in G. It has even length by bipartiteness, and an induced cycle of length at least 10 contains an induced P8 on eight consecutive vertices. Therefore a residual cycle must yield an induced C4, C6, or C8, proving the equivalence. When S is an FVS, each residual component is a tree. A tree of diameter at least seven edges contains an induced P8, so its diameter is at most six and its radius at most three. If S is inclusion-minimal, restoring any x creates a cycle containing x; deleting x from that cycle gives a path between two distinct neighbors of x inside one component of G-S.
claims.witness: A shortest cycle in G-S certifies any failure of the hitting condition; for minimal S, the cycle created by restoring x certifies the two-neighbor property.
claims.search_method: Direct shortest-cycle, tree-diameter, and inclusion-minimality proof, with all parity and inducedness cases checked.

claims.claim: There is an exact parameterized algorithm running in O(8^k n^8) time for solutions of size at most k, as well as a polynomial-time 8-approximation.
claims.evidence: All induced C4, C6, and C8 vertex sets can be enumerated in O(n^8), and Claim 0 identifies FVS solutions exactly with transversals of this rank-eight hypergraph. Branching on every vertex of an unhit hyperedge is exhaustive because every feasible solution must choose one; the search depth is at most k and the number of nodes is O(8^k), giving O(8^k n^8). For approximation, greedily compute a maximal family of pairwise vertex-disjoint listed cycles and return their union U. Maximality implies U hits every listed cycle and hence is an FVS. If the packing has p cycles, every FVS has at least p vertices, while |U| is at most 8p, establishing the factor eight.
claims.witness: The branching tree is certified by an unhit hyperedge at every internal node; a maximal disjoint short-cycle packing certifies the approximation bound.
claims.search_method: Exact reduction to bounded-rank hypergraph transversal followed by a complete branching and packing analysis.

claims.claim: Every C4-free P8-free bipartite graph has treewidth at most 13. Consequently, Feedback Vertex Set is polynomial-time solvable on this subclass.
claims.evidence: If such a graph had a 15-vertex simple path, the subgraph induced by those vertices would have a Hamilton path in that order. Its path edges are mandatory and bipartiteness allows only opposite-parity chords. Because C4-freeness and P8-freeness are hereditary, every prefix must survive the exact extension enumeration. The persisted checker exhaustively tries every allowed chord subset, rejects exactly graphs with a C4 or induced P8, and reproduces the survivor counts 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0 for orders 1 through 15. Thus no 15-vertex simple path exists. In an undirected DFS forest, every edge has ancestor-comparable endpoints. Taking each vertex together with all its DFS ancestors as a bag covers every edge, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form its descendant subtree. Root-to-leaf paths have at most 14 vertices, so bags have size at most 14 and the width is at most 13. A deletion-subset plus connectivity-partition dynamic program on this fixed-width decomposition computes an exact minimum FVS in polynomial time.
claims.witness: The complete survivor-count certificate is 1,1,1,1,1,2,3,5,7,10,10,11,6,3,0, with no admissible ordered graph at order 15.
claims.search_method: Complete integer/bitset enumeration of Hamilton-path-ordered graphs, followed by an independent DFS tree-decomposition proof.

claims.claim: More generally, Feedback Vertex Set is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by the minimum number r of vertices meeting every C4; a concrete bound is 4^r·2^{O(r log r)}·n^{O(1)}.
claims.evidence: For a detected C4, every C4-transversal must contain one of its four vertices. Depth-bounded branching on those vertices, with iterative deepening, therefore finds a minimum transversal X of size r in O(4^r n^{O(1)}) time. The hereditary graph G-X is C4-free, P8-free, and bipartite, so Claim 2 supplies a width-13 decomposition. Adding X to every bag covers all edges involving X and gives width at most r+13. On a nice decomposition, an exact FVS dynamic program stores the deleted boundary subset and the connectivity partition of retained boundary vertices. Introduce-edge transitions reject edges whose endpoints are already connected, and join transitions reject precisely unions whose boundary connectivity creates a cycle. There are at most 2^{O(r log r)} states and state pairs per bag. Combining this with the transversal search gives the stated FPT upper bound.
claims.witness: A minimum C4-transversal X together with the DFS decomposition of G-X, enlarged by X in every bag, is the structural certificate used by the dynamic program.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive four-way transversal branching, verified width reduction, and explicit connectivity-partition state analysis.

claims.claim: Several natural routes from these reductions to the full result are blocked by explicit P8-free families: C4-transversal number is unbounded even after removing false twins; 2-connected C4-free blocks have unbounded order; and the short-cycle LP is not integral.
claims.evidence: In the half graph H_n, neighborhoods are strictly nested on each shore and nonempty neighborhoods on opposite shores contain different vertex types, so there are no false twins. It is 2K2-free and hence P5-free. Retaining all B vertices and a_{n-1},a_n is C4-free, giving a transversal of size n-2. Conversely, if a retained C4-free subgraph has at least two A vertices, let i<j be its two smallest retained A-indices. It retains at most n-j+2 A vertices and at most j B vertices, since two retained B-indices at least j would form a C4 with a_i,a_j. Thus at most n+2 vertices remain; the case of at most one retained A is smaller. Hence the optimum is exactly n-2. For m at least two, the union of m internally disjoint length-three u-v paths has 2m+2 vertices, is bipartite and remains connected after any single-vertex deletion. Every cycle uses two branches and has length six, so it is C4-free. An induced path containing both hubs has at most one extra vertex beyond each hub because a further branch vertex would create a chord to the other hub; paths omitting a hub are shorter. Thus it is P8-free. Finally, K3,3 is P4-free. Deleting one vertex leaves a C4, while deleting two vertices from one shore leaves a forest, so its integral FVS optimum is two. Assigning 1/4 to every vertex satisfies every induced-C4 constraint and has exact objective 3/2, proving nonintegrality.
claims.witness: The explicit witnesses are the half graphs H_n, the length-three theta graphs with m branches, and K3,3 with the all-1/4 fractional assignment.
claims.search_method: Symbolic proofs for all family sizes, supplemented by exhaustive finite graph checks and exact rational arithmetic.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on every P8-free bipartite graph. The draft does not establish that result: O(8^k n^8) is exponential when the solution size k grows, the 8-approximation is not exact, the polynomial-time algorithm applies only to C4-free instances, and the r-parameterized algorithm can be superpolynomial when the minimum C4-transversal r grows with n. These are correct and material structural and algorithmic advances, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, and its final writeup explicitly states that the full target remains unsolved; that resolution claim is therefore ACCURATE.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and iteration-6 draft JSON as source material; used no web, retrieval database, receipt, prior run, report, or other solution.
